newsitem.title: USA: Record industry faces FTC inquiry on pricing - sources.
newsitem.headline: Record industry faces FTC inquiry on pricing - sources.

text.p: The Federal Trade Commission (FTC), which has a long history of monitoring the music business, has launched another probe of the pricing policies of the six major record labels, industry sources said Monday.
"All six labels got an FTC notice last month saying it was opening a preliminary inquiry into minimium advertising price (MAP) policies," said one executive with a major label.

The FTC declined comment, but record industry sources said the agency was investigating the policies under which labels allocate cooperative advertising dollars and free goods to retailers and whether record companies were creating an artificial floor to prices.
Spokesman at the major labels, including Time Warner Inc. Sony Corp., Seagram Co. Ltd.'s Universal Music Group, Polygram NV, Bertelsmann AG and EMI Music, were either unavailable or declined comment.
The inquiry comes at a time when the $12 billion recording industry is facing lagging sales amid overcapacity at the retail level and cut-throat price wars.
Industry sources said the FTC's latest inquiry comes just seven months after it ended a similar three-year inquiry, which ended without the agency taking any action.
The FTC has been instrumental in regulating the music business for many years.
"The FTC has a history of monitoring trade practices in the record industry," said Thomas White, an artists' rights expert, who represents the estates of several performers including Fred Astaire.

White said the FTC played a key role in uncovering and prosecuting industry members during the "payola" scandal of the late 1950s, which involved labels paying money and gifts in exchange for radio airplay.
The agency also blocked a merger in the early 1980s between two industry giants Polygram and Warner.
Top selling CDs typically sell for between $12 and $16 each. Before the latest inquiry, the industry has faced several lawsuits alleging prices are inflated.
